affected_boundaries: table of contents to document body

observed_behavior: The first chapter began in unused space at the bottom of the final table-of-contents page.
expected_behavior: The first chapter and every subsequent top-level chapter begin on fresh pages.
causal_mechanism: Pandoc's stock LaTeX template emits the table of contents immediately before the body, and the composed body had no leading page break; LaTeX therefore flowed chapter 1 into remaining table-of-contents space.

anti_pattern.structural_description: Document pagination relied on incidental source-file boundaries while the template-to-body boundary and top-level heading boundaries had no explicit pagination invariant.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: LaTeX continues normal vertical flow after the table of contents and can place a top-level heading wherever space remains; multiple top-level headings in one source file also bypass file-level separators.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: The generated body begins with a clear page and every top-level heading after the first is preceded by a clear page.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: The composer emits \clearpage at the body boundary and before each subsequent level-one Markdown heading, independently of source-file placement.

applicability_conditions: A Pandoc LaTeX document includes a table of contents and expects chapter-level page starts.
Top-level chapters are represented by level-one Markdown headings.
known_non_matches: Output formats whose templates already force a page break between the table of contents and body.
confirmation_evidence: pandoc -D latex showed \tableofcontents followed directly by $body$ with no page break.
The corrected UAT PDF ended its table of contents on physical page 3, began chapter 1 on page 4, ended chapter 1 on page 5, and began chapter 2 on page 6.
regression_proofs: tests/pm-pdf.test.js: ponytail pm pdf renders configured collections in index order
